1.title: Networking Appliances, Applications and Functions
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Networking Appliances, Applications and Functions. It covers the exam area one point zero Networking Concepts. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. one point two Compare and contrast networking appliances, applications and functions: physical and virtual appliances (router, switch, firewall, I D S or I P S, load balancer, proxy, N A S, S A N, wireless access point and controller). Applications (C D N). Functions (V P N, Qo S, T T L). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one point zero Networking Concepts (twenty-three percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Appliances
1.text: Appliances. Each can be a physical device or a virtual appliance (software on a hypervisor or in the cloud).

1.title: Appliances, continued
1.text: Appliances. The figure shows this: Where each appliance sits between users, the internet and servers.

1.title: Appliances, continued
1.text: Appliances. Router. Connects networks and forwards packets by I P address (layer three). Switch. Connects devices in a L A N and forwards frames by M A C address (layer two). Firewall. Allows or blocks traffic by rules; stateful firewalls track sessions; next-generation firewalls inspect applications and users. I D S (intrusion detection system). Detects and alerts on suspicious traffic; passive (monitors a copy). I P S (intrusion prevention system). Detects and blocks suspicious traffic; inline. Load balancer. Spreads requests across several servers, checks their health.

1.title: Appliances, continued
1.text: Appliances. Proxy. Intermediary for requests: forward proxy (clients to internet, filtering and caching), reverse proxy (internet to servers). Network-attached storage (N A S). File-level storage shared over the L A N (S M B, N F S (Network File System)). Storage area network (S A N). Block-level storage over a dedicated network (Fibre Channel or i S C S I). Access point (A P). Connects wireless clients to the wired network. Wireless controller. Manages many A P s centrally (configuration, channels, roaming). Exam tip: I D S alerts; I P S blocks. N A S equals files; S A N equals blocks. A reverse proxy protects servers; a forward proxy controls clients.

1.title: Applications and functions
1.text: Applications and functions. Content delivery network (C D N). Geographically distributed servers that cache content near users, cutting latency and origin load. Virtual private network (V P N). Encrypted tunnel over a public network (Module sixteen). Quality of service (Qo S). Prioritizes traffic (voice and video before bulk transfers) using classification and queuing. Time to live (T T L). A counter in the I P header reduced by one at each router hop; at zero the packet is dropped (stops routing loops); also the cache lifetime of a D N S record. Exam tip: "Prioritize voice over file transfers" equals Qo S. "Reduce latency for global users of a website" equals C D N. "A packet is discarded after too many hops" equals T T L.

1.title: Applications and functions, continued
1.text: Applications and functions. Exam tip: A firewall decides by rules; a proxy acts on behalf of a client or server; a load balancer chooses a server. Match the verb to the device.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company wants a device that blocks detected attacks inline instead of only alerting. What should it deploy? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: An intrusion prevention system. An I P S sits inline and blocks threats; an I D S only alerts.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Video calls stutter whenever large backups run. What feature should the engineer configure? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Quality of service to prioritize the voice and video traffic. Qo S gives priority to latency-sensitive traffic.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An organization needs shared files accessible over the L A N using S M B (Server Message Block). Which device fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A network-attached storage device. N A S provides file-level storage over the network.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which device distributes client requests across several web servers and removes failed servers from rotation? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A load balancer. Load balancers distribute requests and monitor server health.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A packet's T T L reaches zero at a router. What happens? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The router discards the packet. Packets with an expired T T L are dropped.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company must manage fifty access points from one console. Which component fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A wireless controller. Controllers manage many A P s centrally.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. At which layer does a switch forward frames? Answer: Layer two. Question two. What does a C D N do? Answer: Caches content on servers near users to reduce latency. Question three. What is the difference between N A S and S A N? Answer: N A S is file-level storage; S A N is block-level storage.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does Qo S do? Answer: Prioritizes certain traffic over other traffic. Question five. What does a reverse proxy protect? Answer: The servers behind it. Question six. What reduces T T L by one? Answer: Each router the packet passes through.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Devices: router (L three), switch (L two), firewall (rules), I D S (alert), I P S (block). Traffic managers: load balancer, forward proxy, reverse proxy. Storage: N A S (files), S A N (blocks). Wireless: A P, controller. Functions: C D N, V P N (virtual private network), Qo S, T T L.
